layout.title: Suspension bridge

shows.does: a long wooden plank lies across the river, a rubber duck floats down the river under it
a car rolls onto the plank and the plank snaps in two
two red towers rise on the banks, cables drape over them and the deck hangs from them
a glowing line traces the towers, cables and deck
white wind arrows blow and the light hanging deck twists over
deep steel trusses appear along the deck and it lies flat again
yellow arrows pull the tower tops inward and both towers tip toward the river
concrete anchors appear on both banks with back cables to the tower tops, the towers stand straight
the cables drag both concrete anchors across the ground toward the river
each anchor grows into a huge block of concrete and slides back into place
the towers are pushed down into the soft bank and the ground crumbles at their feet
concrete footings reach down from the towers to the rock and the towers rise back
the deck is paved and rails go up along it, the duck bobbing in the river below
a car drives across the finished suspension bridge over the river, the duck below

layout.why: A wide river in its own valley (terrain with a riverbed, the river there from the first frame), a rubber duck drifting down it. The load's path is the story: a plank snaps under a car, towers and cables hang the deck, the wind twists it, a truss stiffens it, the heavier deck tips the towers, anchors tie the cables back, the cables drag the anchors, bigger anchors hold, the towers sink into the bank, footings reach rock; a car drives across at the end. The camera opens on the plank, then holds the bridge's front with the river and the footings in section.

sentences.text: If you lay a plank across a river, you have a bridge.
But a car rolls on and snaps the plank.
So you hang the deck from cables over two towers.
But wind twists the light hanging deck.
So you stiffen the deck with a truss.
But the heavy truss pulls the towers inward.
So you tie the cables to concrete anchors.
But the cables drag the anchors toward the river.
So you make each anchor weigh 60,000 tons.
But the anchored cables push the towers into the bank.
So you sink the tower footings to solid rock.
Pave the deck and add rails along the river.
Congratulations, a car drives across your suspension bridge.

recurring.what: a rubber duck floating down the river

chain.stakes: the car falls in the river

chain.shows: wind twists the light hanging deck
chain.stakes: the deck tears apart like the Tacoma Narrows Bridge

chain.shows: the heavy truss pulls the cables and both towers tip inward
chain.stakes: the towers fall into the river

chain.shows: the cables drag the concrete anchors toward the river
chain.stakes: the whole bridge sags into the river

chain.shows: the anchored cables push the towers down into the soft bank
chain.stakes: the towers sink and the deck drops

ideas.idea: a plank across a river is already a bridge
a car is too heavy for a long plank and it snaps
two towers carry cables and the deck hangs from them
the light hanging deck twists in the wind
a deep steel truss makes the deck stiff
the heavy truss pulls on the cables and tips the towers inward
the cables are tied back to concrete anchors
the cables pull so hard they drag the anchors toward the river
each anchor is made enormously heavy
held by the anchors, the cables push the towers down into the soft bank
footings carry the towers down to solid rock
the deck is paved and rails go along it over the river
a car drives across the finished suspension bridge
